accepted.s: Who founded the Telugu Desam Party (TDP)?
accepted.x: The Telugu Desam Party was founded by N. T. Rama Rao.
accepted.tq: Use direct founder identification without confusing founders of Andhra Pradesh-based parties.
accepted.sec: AP regional parties - founder and founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Telugu Desam Party was founded on which date?
accepted.x: The TDP was founded on 29 March 1982.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact founding date from the party’s first electoral victory.
accepted.sec: AP regional parties - founder and founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Praja Rajyam Party — K. Chandrashekar Rao — 2008
Telangana Rashtra Samithi — Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy — 2001
accepted.x: The Lok Satta Party was founded by Jayaprakash Narayan in 2006. Praja Rajyam was founded by Chiranjeevi, Jana Sena by Pawan Kalyan, and TRS by K. Chandrashekar Rao.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure founder-year pair and eliminate swapped identities.
accepted.sec: AP regional parties - founder and founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding political parties associated with Andhra Pradesh:
1. Praja Rajyam Party was founded by Chiranjeevi.
2. Praja Rajyam Party merged with the Indian National Congress in 2011.
3. Telangana Rashtra Samithi was founded in 2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Praja Rajyam was founded by Chiranjeevi, merged with Congress in 2011, and TRS was founded in 2001.
accepted.tq: Check each party event separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: AP regional parties - founder and founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Praja Shanti Party — Y. S. Sharmila
YSR Congress Party — Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy
Praja Shanti Party — K. A. Paul
Mahajana Socialist Party — Manda Krishna Madiga
accepted.x: Praja Shanti Party was founded by K. A. Paul. Y. S. Sharmila founded the YSR Telangana Party, not the Praja Shanti Party.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped founder in a closely related party pair.
accepted.sec: AP regional parties - founder and founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The founding of the Telugu Desam Party in 1982 was associated primarily with which idea?
o: Telugu self-respect or Telugu atma gauravam
accepted.x: N. T. Rama Rao founded the TDP around the idea of Telugu self-respect, in response to perceived slights from the Centre.
accepted.tq: Identify the party-specific slogan or political basis rather than a neighbouring regional issue.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Telugu Desam Party came to power within approximately how long of its formation?
accepted.x: The TDP won power in the January 1983 Assembly election, roughly nine months after its formation, marking one of the fastest rises of a political party.
accepted.tq: Separate the short interval between formation and victory from the election year itself.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
N. T. Rama Rao served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during which of the following periods?
1. 1983–84
2. 1984–89
3. 1994–95
accepted.x: N. T. Rama Rao served as Chief Minister during all three periods: 1983–84, 1984–89 and 1994–95.
accepted.tq: Verify every period instead of assuming that successive terms form one continuous tenure.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which regional party became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha in 1984?
accepted.x: With 30 seats in 1984, the TDP became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha and was the first regional party to attain that position.
accepted.tq: Link the party, election year, seat figure and parliamentary status.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The TDP won how many seats in the 1984 Lok Sabha election when it became the main opposition party?
accepted.x: The TDP won 30 seats in 1984 and consequently became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical figure attached to a parliamentary achievement.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the chairman of the National Front in 1988, which formed the V. P. Singh government in 1989?
accepted.x: N. T. Rama Rao was chairman of the National Front in 1988; the National Front formed the V. P. Singh government in 1989.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the coalition’s chairman from the Prime Minister it subsequently supported.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the ideological orientation of the Telugu Desam Party as stated in the material?
o: No specific ideology beyond Telugu pride and welfare populism
A programme centred only on religious mobilisation
A specific Marxist ideology combined with linguistic nationalism
accepted.x: The TDP did not espouse a specific ideology beyond Telugu pride and welfare populism.
accepted.tq: Avoid replacing a broad political orientation with an unrelated ideological label.
accepted.sec: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: DMK — Tamil Nadu — C. N. Annadurai — 1949
Shiv Sena — Maharashtra — M. G. Ramachandran — 1966
Biju Janata Dal — Bihar — Naveen Patnaik — 1997
accepted.x: The DMK was founded in Tamil Nadu by C. N. Annadurai in 1949. The other options interchange founders or States.
accepted.tq: Start with the complete party-State-founder-year combination and reject swapped pairs.
accepted.sec: Regional parties across India - state and founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The AIADMK was founded by M. G. Ramachandran in 1972.
2. Shiv Sena was founded by Bal Thackeray in Maharashtra in 1966.
3. The Jannayak Janta Party was founded by Dushyant Chautala in Haryana in 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: AIADMK–M. G. Ramachandran–1972, Shiv Sena–Bal Thackeray–1966, and JJP–Dushyant Chautala–2018.
accepted.tq: Test several complete party-founder-State-year associations together.
accepted.sec: Regional parties across India - state and founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rashtriya Janata Dal — Bihar — Lalu Prasad Yadav — 1997
Biju Janata Dal — Odisha — Naveen Patnaik — 1997
accepted.x: The Shiromani Akali Dal was founded in Punjab in 1920, not 1985. Asom Gana Parishad was founded in Assam in 1985.
accepted.tq: Spot the altered year while retaining the correct party and State.
accepted.sec: Regional parties across India - state and founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The DMK originally demanded which of the following and later formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under C. N. Annadurai?
accepted.x: The DMK began with anti-Brahmin, anti-North and anti-Hindi positions and demanded Dravidanadu; it later scaled back these demands and formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under Annadurai.
accepted.tq: Connect the original demand with the party’s later electoral transition.
accepted.sec: Regional parties across India - state and founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The slogan associated with Shiv Sena’s regional mobilisation was
o: Autonomy for West Bengal through Centre-State memoranda
Bombay for Maharashtrians, along with jobs for sons of the soil
Telugu atma gauravam and welfare populism
accepted.x: Shiv Sena mobilised around the idea of “Bombay for Maharashtrians” and the demand for jobs for the sons of the soil.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the distinctive regional slogans of different parties.
accepted.sec: Regional parties across India - state and founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following political parties in chronological order of their founding:
A. Bahujan Samaj Party
B. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
C. Telugu Desam Party
D. Shiv Sena
accepted.x: The correct order is DMK (1949), Shiv Sena (1966), TDP (1982) and BSP (1984).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest parties first, then place the middle entries by year.
accepted.sec: Regional parties in chronological order of founding  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the founding order of the parties from 1985 onwards?
o: AGP, Samajwadi Party, BJD and RJD, TRS, YSRCP
Samajwadi Party, AGP, BJD and RJD, YSRCP, TRS
AGP, BJD and RJD, Samajwadi Party, TRS, YSRCP
BJD and RJD, AGP, Samajwadi Party, TRS, YSRCP
accepted.x: The sequence is AGP (1985), Samajwadi Party (1992), BJD and RJD (1997), TRS (2001), and YSRCP (2011).
accepted.tq: Use the years to order the closely spaced later regional parties.
accepted.sec: Regional parties in chronological order of founding  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following parties was founded earliest?
accepted.x: The DMK was founded in 1949, earlier than the BSP in 1984, TDP in 1982 and Samajwadi Party in 1992.
accepted.tq: Identify the earliest item by comparing the founding years directly.
accepted.sec: Regional parties in chronological order of founding  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which committee was appointed by the DMK government of Tamil Nadu to examine Centre-State relations?
accepted.x: The DMK government of Tamil Nadu appointed the Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations in 1969; its report was submitted in 1971.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with the party government that initiated it.
accepted.sec: Autonomy demands - party and document  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Rajamannar Committee — DMK government of Tamil Nadu — 1969
2. Anandpur Sahib Resolution — Shiromani Akali Dal — 1973
3. Memorandum on Centre-State relations — CPI(M)-led West Bengal government — 1977
accepted.x: All three associations are correct. The Rajamannar Committee was appointed in 1969, the Anandpur Sahib Resolution dates to 1973, and the West Bengal memorandum was issued in 1977.
accepted.tq: Check each autonomy-related document against its political sponsor and year.
accepted.sec: Autonomy demands - party and document  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is included among the national parties listed in the material?
1. Bharatiya Janata Party
2. Indian National Congress
3. National People’s Party
4. Trinamool Congress
accepted.x: The listed national parties include BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP. Trinamool Congress is identified among State or unrecognised parties in the cited list.
accepted.tq: Separate listed national parties from regional or unrecognised parties.
accepted.sec: Regional vs national parties - identify, states ruled  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is classified as a State or unrecognised party rather than one of the national parties listed?
accepted.x: The Telugu Desam Party is included among the State or unrecognised parties in the cited list, whereas AAP, BSP and NPP are listed as national parties.
accepted.tq: Use elimination between national-party names and a prominent regional party.
accepted.sec: Regional vs national parties - identify, states ruled  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which set correctly identifies the States or territories where the BJP defeated the regional parties named in the cited sequence?
o: BJD in Odisha, AAP in Delhi and Trinamool Congress in West Bengal
BJD in Bihar, AAP in Punjab and Trinamool Congress in Assam
BJD in Andhra Pradesh, AAP in Gujarat and Trinamool Congress in Odisha
BJD in West Bengal, AAP in Odisha and Trinamool Congress in Delhi
accepted.x: The cited sequence states that the BJP defeated BJD in Odisha in 2024, AAP in Delhi in 2025 and Trinamool Congress in West Bengal in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match each party with the State or territory associated with its electoral defeat.
accepted.sec: Regional vs national parties - identify, states ruled  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a basis or cause for the rise of regional parties?
o: Failure of national parties to accommodate State leaders
Uniform economic development across all regions
accepted.x: The identified causes include linguistic and cultural identity, regional economic neglect, and the failure of national parties to accommodate State leaders. Uniform development is not listed as a cause.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated cause of regional mobilisation.
accepted.sec: Rise of regional parties - linguistic, caste and regional bases

accepted.s: Which of the following factors strengthened the importance of regional parties after 1989?
o: Uniform dominance of one national party in every State
Coalition arithmetic at the national level
accepted.x: After 1989, coalition arithmetic increased the national importance of regional parties because their parliamentary support could determine government formation and survival.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-effect link between fragmented mandates and coalition influence.
accepted.sec: Rise of regional parties - linguistic, caste and regional bases

accepted.s:
Regionalism in India has been described as having which combination of roots?
1. Historical
2. Geographical
3. Linguistic
4. Religious and ethnic
accepted.x: The identified roots of regionalism are historical, geographical, linguistic, religious and ethnic. Linguistic diversity includes the presence of 22 Scheduled Languages.
accepted.tq: Prefer the comprehensive combination when every listed dimension is supported.
accepted.sec: Rise of regional parties - linguistic, caste and regional bases

accepted.s: The politically awakened non-Brahmin agrarian castes in Andhra during the Justice Party era included
accepted.x: The Andhra non-Brahmin agrarian castes identified as becoming politically awakened during the Justice Party era were Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete caste grouping rather than selecting a partly familiar list.
accepted.sec: Rise of regional parties - linguistic, caste and regional bases

accepted.s: Which of the following is a consequence of the rise of regional parties in coalition politics?
o: They transferred all legislative powers to local bodies.
They prevented all coalition governments after 1989.
They have sometimes acted as kingmakers and supplied Speakers, Union Ministers and survival votes.
They eliminated the need for bargaining between the Centre and the States.
accepted.x: Regional parties have acted as coalition kingmakers, supplied Speakers and Union Ministers, and provided votes necessary for government survival.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical parliamentary consequences of coalition dependence.
accepted.sec: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands

accepted.s: The rise of regional parties made Indian federalism more genuinely bargained, particularly after
accepted.x: The material links more genuine federal bargaining to the period after 1989, when coalition politics increased the negotiating power of regional parties.
accepted.tq: Connect the turning-point year with the institutional change it signifies.
accepted.sec: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states both a positive and a negative impact of regional parties?
o: End of coalition politics; strengthening of one-party rule
Reduced representation and slower development; political permanence
Centralisation and uniformity; elimination of regional demands
Backward-region representation and balanced development; parochialism and instability
accepted.x: Regional parties can improve representation of backward regions and promote balanced development, but may also encourage parochialism and instability.
accepted.tq: Match the positive and negative columns without reversing their direction.
accepted.sec: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands

accepted.s: The demand for Special Category Status mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh concerns
o: The State of Telangana immediately after 1956
Tamil Nadu after the formation of the DMK government
The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after 2014
accepted.x: The demand for Special Category Status was raised for the residuary Andhra Pradesh after 2014.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the residuary State formed after bifurcation from other States associated with autonomy demands.
accepted.sec: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands

accepted.s: Why did the Telugu Desam Party leave the National Democratic Alliance in 2018?
o: Over opposition to the Anandpur Sahib Resolution
Over the demand for Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh
Over the appointment of the Rajamannar Committee
accepted.x: The TDP left the NDA in 2018 over the demand for Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Link the party’s coalition decision to the specific federal demand that triggered it.
accepted.sec: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands
